title: Shopify Drops React Native for Swift and Kotlin as AI Changes Cross-Platform Development Tradeoffs
gist: Shopify is abandoning React Native — which it declared its mobile future in 2020 and reaffirmed in 2025 — to rewrite its flagship apps natively in Swift/SwiftUI and Kotlin/Jetpack Compose, because Head of Mobile Mustafa Ali judged that AI coding agents have inverted the cost/benefit of maintaining two native codebases. Six engineers rebuilt the Shop app to production in 12 weeks, yielding 23-50% faster cold start, a 10x drop in crashing sessions and 75% faster Android release builds.

themes.theme: AI inverts the cross-platform cost equation

insights.claim: Shopify's Head of Mobile Mustafa Ali reassessed the company's React Native commitment on the explicit thesis that improved AI model quality pushed the benefit/cost ratio of maintaining separate native codebases above that of using a cross-platform abstraction layer.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: If agents make duplicate-codebase maintenance cheap, the core economic rationale for cross-platform frameworks (write once) erodes — a structural risk to the React Native/Flutter ecosystem and the vendors around it.
insights.quote: estimating that the benefit/cost ratio of maintaining native codebases across mobile platforms was now above that of using an abstraction layer
insights.locator: Shopify recently announced it is abandoning React Native

insights.claim: The reversal came fast: Shopify declared React Native the future of its mobile architecture in 2020 and reaffirmed that commitment in 2025 after completing a five-year migration of all its apps, then abandoned it a little over a year later.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Platform commitments that took five years to execute are now being unwound in roughly one — shortening the useful life of any framework bet and raising the discount on developer-tooling lock-in.
insights.locator: The about-face shift comes after Shopify declared in 2020

insights.claim: A single engineer's one-week proof of concept was enough to justify a full greenfield rewrite over an incremental migration, and six engineers then rebuilt the flagship Shop app from scratch to production deployment in 12 weeks.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Agent-assisted rewrites at this speed make 'rewrite rather than migrate' a live option for large codebases, undermining the migration-tooling and modernization-services value proposition.
insights.quote: six engineers rebuilt the flagship Shop app from the ground up to production deployment in 12 weeks
insights.locator: The second factor was the fast-paced improvement in quality of AI coding models

insights.claim: The trigger for the re-evaluation was not AI alone but a looming forced refactor: adopting React Native's New Architecture would have required revisiting native module integrations, rendering, and the shared/platform-specific code boundary anyway.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Framework breaking changes are the moment incumbents lose users — watch upgrade-forcing releases as churn events for any developer platform.
insights.quote: That work would have required us to revisit native module integrations, rendering, and the boundaries between shared and platform-specific code
insights.locator: The first was a looming significant refactor

insights.claim: Shopify reports that going native cut cold startup latency by 23% on iOS and 50% on Android, and improved session stability from 99.5% to 99.95% — a 10x reduction in crashing sessions.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Concrete conversion-relevant metrics (startup, crash rate) give other consumer-app operators a quantified case to reopen their own framework decisions.
insights.quote: dropping 23% on iOS and 50% on Android
insights.locator: Shopify reports improvement in cold startup latency

insights.claim: On Android the native rewrite delivered 75% faster release build times and sustained 120 FPS feed scrolling without extensive manual optimization.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Build-time gains compound into developer throughput; 120 FPS out of the box weakens the 'good enough' defense of abstraction layers on high-refresh devices.
insights.quote: native feed scrolling maintained sustained 120 FPS throughput without requiring extensive manual optimization
insights.locator: Shopify reports improvement in cold startup latency

insights.claim: Even in 2020 Shopify's React Native apps were reported as fast (<500ms screen loads) and stable (>99.9% crash-free sessions), so the new native numbers are an improvement on an already-good baseline rather than a rescue of a failing stack.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: The switch was driven by changed economics, not by framework failure — don't read it as evidence that cross-platform cannot ship quality apps.
insights.locator: Shopify at the time reported increased development productivity

insights.claim: Shopify standardized on the declarative UI frameworks SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose specifically to exploit structural and mental-model symmetries between iOS and Android, making it easier to steer autonomous agents while still matching platform-native idioms.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Framework choice is starting to be optimized for agent legibility rather than human ergonomics — a new selection criterion that favors Apple's and Google's first-party declarative stacks.
insights.locator: By standardizing on modern declarative UI frameworks

insights.claim: Shopify isolated the volatile layers (mobile platform, UI) from stable business logic and state management so agents could dispatch actions, manipulate navigation state and assert outcomes in milliseconds on the desktop without rendering UI or booting a simulator, reserving simulators for end-to-end integration passes.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Feedback-loop latency is the real constraint on agentic coding; architectures that give agents a fast headless oracle are the transferable pattern to watch across domains.
insights.quote: AI models would thus dispatch actions, manipulate navigation state, and assert outcomes in milliseconds, on the desktop, without rendering UI or using a simulator
insights.locator: An interesting detail however is that Shopify isolated the factors of change

insights.claim: Despite the AI leverage, the rewrite still required considerable human engineering in architecture, planning agent work, validating task completion and remediating errors — agents did not remove the senior engineering requirement.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Tempers the headcount-substitution narrative: demand shifts toward architects and validators rather than disappearing.
insights.quote: the rewrite did still require considerable engineering involvement in architecture, planning agent work, validating task completion and remediating errors
insights.locator: In spite of the progress in AI coding models

themes.theme: Contested evidence and native's hidden cost

insights.claim: Critics note Shopify benchmarked native against React Native's old architecture rather than its New Architecture, leaving open the possibility that migrating within React Native could have delivered comparable gains.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Treat the headline performance deltas as directional marketing, not a controlled comparison, before extrapolating to other framework decisions.
insights.locator: One argument is that Shopify’s reported performance and productivity results

insights.claim: The main structural cost of going full native is losing over-the-air updates: shipping changes requires passing app-store review, which slows release frequency and makes rollbacks harder.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: App-store review latency is the tax on native; it directly conflicts with the faster shipping cadence AI codegen is supposed to unlock.
insights.quote: Shipping a new version of the app may require going through the app review process gate, thus slowing down release frequency.
insights.locator: Another significant tradeoff reported by developers

insights.claim: One developer argues that the perceived need for rapid over-the-air changes is itself a cultural artifact of web-background teams, and that native's harder rollbacks push teams toward better release tooling, more deliberate change review and one larger stable release every few weeks.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Suggests release-cadence expectations, not technical limits, drive framework preference — relevant when assessing whether native rewrites spread beyond Shopify.
insights.quote: With native, you know each release is harder to roll back, so you tend to build more tooling around releases, think through changes more carefully, and test more thoroughly before they’re ready to ship.
insights.locator: I’ve worked with both native and cross-platform

insights.claim: Shopify plans to finish the Shopify app — 300+ screens plus home and lockscreen widgets, an Apple Watch app and Siri Shortcuts — this year, with Point of Sale and Inbox following over the coming year.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: A dated delivery commitment on a 300+ screen app is the checkable test of whether agent-assisted rewrite velocity holds at full scale.
insights.locator: Shopify plans to complete its Point of Sale, and Inbox apps

insights.claim: Even at peak React Native commitment Shopify held that native remained the better choice for device-hardware features like 2D/3D scanning, on-device AI models, memory-constrained widgets, Apple Watch apps, App Intents, Siri Shortcuts and long-running background jobs.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: On-device AI and hardware access were already pulling work back to native before agents changed the math — two independent forces pointing the same direction.
insights.quote: Native is still the best way for building cutting-edge features that leverage device hardware like 2D / 3D scanning and running AI models on-device.
insights.locator: Yet, even then, Shopify did not discard native platform development entirely
